svg.title: Who Stands Between a Brand and Delivered SMS
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-06-10dlc-registration-architecture; chapter number: 11; title: Who Stands Between a Brand and Delivered SMS; subtitle: A2P 10DLC registration, vetting and throughput; chart type: org_architecture; center: role: Registered brand; headcount: 1 brand per business; an agency never registers itself as the brand; focus: Opt-in call to action a reviewer can actually see, legal name and EIN matched to IRS records; spokes: role: TCR brand registration; type: Registry; kpi: $4 brand fee; legal name, EIN and DUNS match exactly; role: External vetting provider; type: Vetting (WMC Global, Aegis, campaignverify.org); kpi: $40 one-time; score 80-100 unlocks 4,500 TPM and 200,000 segments/day; role: DCA campaign reviewer; type: Campaign vetting; kpi: $15 per attempt; one MSP needed about 15 attempts; role: Carriers and CPaaS platform; type: Delivery and throttling; kpi: Default 2,000 segments/day T-Mobile, 75 TPM AT&T; internal caps as low as 60 per minute; caption: Registration lives or dies on the opt-in call to action, and throughput is set by the vetting score.; assumptions note: Practitioners disagree on whether resubmissions cost money; Telgorithm reports $15 per DCA attempt while Austin Marland reports no repeat fee.; note: Sources: Telgorithm (dgkKW0cbz1E), TwilioDevs (KWvbRToRnGg, 7pXYEARPIwU), RingLogix (gmCqaG2hBKQ), Paradigm Escape (wpj7_7cz4Kk), Signal House (sVsWkczKncU), Telecom Application Development Summit (SRizDef5BbE).
